# recusata.tsv — the failing set, pinned

**This proves STABILITY, never CORRECTNESS.** It is generated by our
own parser, so it says what we say. Correctness comes from html5lib,
which sits underneath it; this file catches only regression.

## What it is

One line per html5lib case our cooked view does NOT reproduce:

```
<index><TAB><plagula> #<numerus>
```

`<index>` is the case's position in the judged corpus (script-on cases
are omitted, so it is not the raw file index). It exists so the gate
can merge-diff two sets in one pass — both are subsequences of the
same ordered universe, so a lexicographic sort is never needed.

## Why, when a rising number already exists

**A rising pin is a FLOOR, so every regression above it is invisible.**
The pin is raised by hand, so it usually lags the live number; in that
window the gate is blind. Measured 2026-09-19: with the pin at 1504
and 1509 live, removing a real rule dropped one case and the number
assertion still PASSED. Only the set named it.

The sharper case is a change that fixes as many as it breaks: the
total does not move at all. That happened the same day — the template
rule read 1509 against a 1509 baseline while `tests19 #46` was fixed
and `tests19 #82` broken. A gate on the number alone would have called
it "no change".

## Moving it

```
ORACULUM_SCRIBERE=1 ./html/compile_probationes.sh oraculum
```

`SANATA` (a case now passing) fails the gate on purpose. Improvement is
good but must not be absorbed silently: read what moved, then
regenerate and name the cause in the commit — the house rule for every
golden.

A re-vendor of the corpus invalidates every index at once. That is
already a named change to `probatio_html_exempla` (file, byte and case
counts are pinned there); move both together.
